proposals.hypothesis: Li3B(PO4)2 is a Li-rich borophosphate that combines the orthoborate-type B-O framework of the penalty-bin-0 Li4Ca(BO3)2 coating with the phosphate anion of Li3PO4. It should be wide-gap and oxidation-resistant at 4.0 V, and its high Li content may limit Co-O and In/Cl interfacial reactions. It tests whether a mixed borate/phosphate Li-rich framework keeps the low penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 5 eV), electronically insulating Li-ion conductor with high oxidative stability. It is a well-known cathode coating that should suppress Co-O/chloride interfacial reactions at 4.0 V while still passing Li ions. Its Li-rich, phosphate chemistry is also relatively compatible with a Li3InCl6 contact.

Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich borate with good oxidative stability. Like Li3PO4, it should block electron transfer at the LiCoO2 interface at 4.0 V while passing Li ions. Its Li-rich chemistry should limit reactivity with the Li3InCl6 contact. This tests a borate family that has not yet been evaluated.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) gave penalty bin 0 with status ok and insulation, so this Li-rich oxyanion family is a plausible low-penalty route. Li3BO3 is a chemically different family, so it is an exploratory check.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3Al(BO3)2 is a Li-rich orthoborate, closely related to the Li3BO3 coating that gave penalty bin 0 with insulation. Replacing B with Al keeps the wide-gap orthoborate anion and high Li content, while Al3+ is more reducing-resistant and less prone to forming Co- or In-containing byproducts at the LiCoO2 and Li3InCl6 interfaces at 4.0 V.
proposal.motivation: Li3BO3 (mp-aaaabojb) gave penalty bin 0, status ok, insulating, with a 5.7 eV gap, so the Li-rich orthoborate family looks promising. Li3PO4 was penalty bin 15, so phosphate is less favorable.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4Ca(BO3)2 is a Li-rich orthoborate, the same anion family as Li3Al(BO3)2, which gave penalty bin 0 with insulation and a 5.7 eV gap. Swapping the trivalent Al3+ for divalent Ca2+ keeps the wide-gap orthoborate framework and high Li content. It should also be a reductively and oxidatively robust barrier against Co-O and In/Cl interfacial reactions at 4.0 V. The aim is to test whether another Li-rich orthoborate stays in the low-penalty bin.
proposal.motivation: Li3Al(BO3)2 (mp-aaaaajan) gave penalty bin 0, status ok, insulating, and acceptable, while Li3PO4 (bin 15) and Li3BO3 (bin 4) were worse. Li4Ca(BO3)2 is a close orthoborate analog with a similar Li-rich chemistry.
